informal_statement: The equivalence demonstrates that for the system `PureU1 2`, the sets of linear solutions and general solutions are essentially the same. This means that every linear solution is also a solution in the broader sense, and conversely, every solution is inherently a linear solution within this system.
informal_proof: To establish the equivalence between linear solutions and general solutions for the system `PureU1 2`, we define a mapping that transforms linear solutions into general solutions. This mapping is constructed by applying algebraic simplifications and ensuring that the structural properties of the system are preserved. The simplicity of the system, involving only two elements, allows us to handle these transformations without introducing complex dependencies. By verifying that this mapping is bijective—meaning each linear solution uniquely corresponds to a general solution and vice versa—we confirm that the two sets are indeed equivalent under the defined transformation.

id.name: PureU1.Two.equiv
id.content:
/-- An equivalence between `LinSols` and `Sols`. -/
def equiv : (PureU1 2).LinSols ≃ (PureU1 2).Sols where
  toFun S := ⟨⟨S, fun i => Fin.elim0 i⟩, by
    have hLin := pureU1_linear S
    simp only [succ_eq_add_one, reduceAdd, PureU1_numberCharges, Fin.sum_univ_two,
      Fin.isValue] at hLin
    erw [accCube_explicit]
    simp only [Fin.sum_univ_two, Fin.isValue]
    rw [show S.val (0 : Fin 2) = - S.val (1 : Fin 2) from eq_neg_of_add_eq_zero_left hLin]
    ring⟩
  invFun S := S.1.1
  left_inv S := rfl
  right_inv S := rfl

/-- An equivalence between `LinSols` and `Sols`. -/
def equiv : (PureU1 2).LinSols ≃ (PureU1 2).Sols where
  toFun S := ⟨⟨S, fun i => Fin.elim0 i⟩, by
    /-
      n : Nat
      S : (PureU1 2).LinSols
      ⊢ Eq ((PureU1 2).cubicACC { toLinSols := S, quadSol := ⋯ }.val) 0
    -/
    have hLin := pureU1_linear S
    simp only [succ_eq_add_one, reduceAdd, PureU1_numberCharges, Fin.sum_univ_two,
      Fin.isValue] at hLin
    /-
      n : Nat
      S : (PureU1 2).LinSols
      hLin : Eq (HAdd.hAdd (S.val 0) (S.val 1)) 0
      ⊢ Eq ((PureU1 2).cubicACC { toLinSols := S, quadSol := ⋯ }.val) 0
    -/
    erw [accCube_explicit]
    /-
      n : Nat
      S : (PureU1 2).LinSols
      hLin : Eq (HAdd.hAdd (S.val 0) (S.val 1)) 0
      ⊢ Eq (Finset.univ.sum fun i => HPow.hPow ({ toLinSols := S, quadSol := ⋯ }.val …
    -/
    simp only [Fin.sum_univ_two, Fin.isValue]
    /-
      n : Nat
      S : (PureU1 2).LinSols
      hLin : Eq (HAdd.hAdd (S.val 0) (S.val 1)) 0
      ⊢ Eq (HAdd.hAdd (HPow.hPow (S.val 0) 3) (HPow.hPow (S.val 1) 3)) 0
    -/
    rw [show S.val (0 : Fin 2) = - S.val (1 : Fin 2) from eq_neg_of_add_eq_zero_left hLin]
    /-
      n : Nat
      S : (PureU1 2).LinSols
      hLin : Eq (HAdd.hAdd (S.val 0) (S.val 1)) 0
      ⊢ Eq (HAdd.hAdd (HPow.hPow (Neg.neg (S.val 1)) 3) (HPow.hPow (S.val 1) 3)) 0
    -/
    ring⟩
    /-
      🎉 no goals
    -/
  invFun S := S.1.1
  left_inv S := rfl
  right_inv S := rfl

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a
C1_dependencies.compilationAlias:

C1_dependencies.name: PureU1.accCube_explicit
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- The cubic ACC for the pure-`U(1)` anomaly equations is equal to the sum of the cubed
  charges. -/
lemma accCube_explicit (n : ℕ) (S : (PureU1Charges n).Charges) :
    accCube n S = ∑ i : Fin n, S i ^ 3:= by
  rw [accCube, TriLinearSymm.toCubic]
  change accCubeTriLinSymm S S S = _
  rw [accCubeTriLinSymm]
  simp only [PureU1Charges_numberCharges, TriLinearSymm.mk₃_toFun_apply_apply]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => Eq.symm (pow_three' (S x))

C1_dependencies.name: Fin.isValue
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- Simplification procedure for ensuring `Fin n` literals are normalized. -/
builtin_dsimproc [simp, seval] isValue ((OfNat.ofNat _ : Fin _)) := fun e => do
  let_expr OfNat.ofNat _ m _ ← e | return .continue
  let some ⟨n, v⟩ ← getFinValue? e | return .continue
  let some m ← getNatValue? m | return .continue
  if m < n then
    -- Design decision: should we return `.continue` instead of `.done` when simplifying.
    -- In the symbolic evaluator, we must return `.done`, otherwise it will unfold the `OfNat.ofNat`
    return .done e
  return .done <| toExpr v

C1_dependencies.content:
/-- The ACC system for a pure $U(1)$ gauge theory with $n$ fermions. -/
@[simps!]
def PureU1 (n : ℕ) : ACCSystem where
  numberLinear := 1
  linearACCs := fun i =>
    match i with
    | 0 => PureU1.accGrav n
  numberQuadratic := 0
  quadraticACCs := Fin.elim0
  cubicACC := PureU1.accCube n
